title: Mesh-paint albedo (side view, nothing painted yet)
description: The first view to paint: no painted view exists yet, so the design plate is the SECOND image (the mesh-paint step's original behaviour).

body.subject: The FIRST image is a grey clay render of a 3D armor model seen from one side. The SECOND image is the original colour design of the armor seen from this same side.
body.action: Paint the FIRST image: keep every shape of the clay model exactly where it is - same outline, same position, same scale, every plate, lion head, rivet, belt, fold and fringe, pixel for pixel. Do not move, add, remove or redraw any shape; only colour the surfaces that are already there.
body.style: Colours: {{colours}} Output a flat ALBEDO texture: no lighting, no shadows, no shading, no ambient occlusion, no highlights, no reflections, no gloss - every surface only its flat base colour.
body.constraints: Plain flat white background. No text.

colours.default: warm dark bronze-brown plate metal (not black), antique gold lion heads, trims, rims, rivets and ornaments, crimson red cloth with gold Greek-key embroidery bands at the hems, black linen undersuit, oxblood red leather belt.

clay_render.description: the grey clay render of the model

design_plate.description: the original colour design from this same view

openai/gpt-image*.note: GPT Image wants the reference order stated in prose and takes an explicit size (<= 3840 per edge, ~8.3 MP)

black-forest-labs/*.note: takes resolution + aspect_ratio; tolerates shorter prompts
